newsitem.title: UK: NWE LS straight-run easier, HS more active, firm.
newsitem.headline: NWE LS straight-run easier, HS more active, firm.

text.p: Low sulphur straight-run fuel oil slipped on Tuesday as slack demand failed to mop up small parcels said to be available and crude prices fell.
Buyers and sellers were still wide apart, with bids quoted in the mid-$140s fob a tonne and offers closer to $150.

The high sulphur market was more active as two cargoes of Russian straight-run material were traded. An M-100 cargo was seen sold to a European refiner at two means +$4 cif NWE, although one thought the price may have been a shade lower.
Traders also said the same refiner bought an E-4 cargo at around formula +$3.50 a tonne cif NWE.
